entities.summary: Kaṇāda, also known as Kaṇabhaksha, Kaṇabhuj, was an ancient Indian natural scientist and philosopher who founded the Vaisheshika school of Indian philosophy that also represents the earliest Indian physics. Born in the 2nd century BCE, Kaṇāda was a prominent figure in the development of Indian thought during the Classical period. His work, particularly his treatise on logic and epistemology, had a lasting impact on the evolution of Indian philosophy and science.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Kaṇāda's Vaisheshika school of philosophy had a lasting impact on the development of Indian thought and science, shaping the course of classical Indian thought and influencing the work of later Indian philosophers and scientists.
